The suggested retail price has nothing to do with how much a game cost to make and has everything to do with popularity and consumer demand. Big budget games do not cost a set amount on release because they are more expensive to create, they cost that amount because if they were more expensive they could risk losing sales due to consumer willingness to pay. A specific sports title offers a unique gaming experience that is not going to be found elsewhere. Most importantly, besides the mechanics of the game, it features well known characters that are a valuable commodity. Sure you could probably find a wacky version of that sport game on a digital store that’s comparable, but more people will be inclined to pay premium for a game that features characters that they recognize, increasing the consumers willingness to pay for the game. The publisher can also get away with selling their games at a higher price for several reasons, including a unique market position compared to competitors. Games on competitor systems have to share the market with many more third party developers than this publisher because they have more third party support. This is also why you might see a price drop for a major game well before a game from this publisher released on the same day. A major competitor will want to drop the price so their product remains competitive with newer games coming out past its release, but this publisher won’t because their games retain value relative to the newer games on their system as well as the games available on other consoles for different reasons.
